findings.reason: a node built exactly as written ships a station that silently ignores the output and the verdict movement of every resumed, lane-changed and promoted run, and none of s6's three-tick measures exercises a run whose stream is not its pointer's `log_path`, so the gate would pass with the defect in place.
findings.text: s6 states "The classifier … runs once per run whose classification inputs changed, keyed on `recovery_memo._classification_inputs`, which covers the pointer, the stream, the manifest, the run directory's records, the review-store candidates and the tree head", but `_classification_inputs` (reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py:450-480) stats `record["log_path"]` only, whereas the production gate `_snapshot_reuse_key` (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:1029-1069) adds the newest stream on purpose — "The newest stream a run has may differ from the pointer's own log once a resume or a lane change writes beside it" (`_record_newest_stream`, reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:432-436, "a resumed or lane-changed run … is writing now rather than the one it started with") — and the promotion ledger row, "because a promotion writes it while the pointer still exists and no other input moves with it"; the same narrowing is in the store's stream discovery, where `StationStore._pointer_streams` (reckon/crew/station_store.py:338-352) yields one stream per pointer and would never ingest a resumed run's new stream at all

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s6 keys the classifier's change gate on `recovery_memo._classification_inputs`, which covers only the pointer's own `log_path`, while the production gate already in use (`recovery_watch._snapshot_reuse_key`) composes that key *plus* the run's newest stream and its promotion ledger row; a resumed, lane-changed or promoted run would therefore never be reclassified.
